scope: CLI args, forwarding create/edit, groups/selectors, ports/names; read-only source audit

rounds.result: Five distinct issues reproduced; dynamic explicit replacement recorded as non-finding.
Two additional listener-overlap issues; IPv6 roundtrip, invalid syntax, name collisions/truncation and batch/edit atomicity checked.
Full remaining CLI creation/edit/selection/port/name matrix plus issue-driven overlap proof; no additional distinct issues beyond CLI-N1..N7.

findings.title: Numeric/range-looking rule names are swallowed as direction values when options precede NAME
findings.expected: edit --remote 1234 and edit 1234 --remote should select the same existing rule; explicit legacy values need unambiguous handling

findings.title: Local/remote full mapping edit with omitted optional bind resets IPv6/custom bind to 127.0.0.1
findings.expected: Preserve unspecified bind during edits as help promises. Dynamic replacement has separately documented replacement semantics, recorded as an observation rather than a separate defect.

findings.title: Bracketed invalid IPv6 destination literals are saved and pass config validate
findings.expected: Reject malformed bracketed IPv6 literals at parse/save time instead of deferring an inevitable destination failure until traffic arrives

findings.title: Names and groups may collide with stable IDs, so ID-based commands operate on the wrong object
findings.expected: Enforce unambiguous ID/name/group namespaces or prioritize and explicitly disambiguate IDs; a printed stable ID must reliably address its own rule/server

findings.title: Automatic group truncation silently merges batches from distinct long server names
findings.expected: Automatic group names must remain distinct across server profiles or reject an incompatible automatic-group collision with a clear message

findings.title: IPv4 wildcard is treated as conflicting with an IPv6-specific listener in the same group
findings.expected: IPv4 0.0.0.0 and a specific IPv6 ::1 listener are distinct address families; do not reject this valid dual-stack layout. IPv6 wildcard dual-stack behavior may conservatively conflict with IPv4.

findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 and IPv4 listeners sharing one port pass group validation despite binding the same socket namespace
findings.expected: Normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 before listener overlap checks; refuse a group that cannot start together
